title: Queue hard-stop cascade: continuous-batcher stall, tail latency spikes, and fairness regression — mitigations & operator playbook
creator: Aisha Khan
description: During a weekday traffic surge we observed a rapid cascade where an internal queue hit a hard-stop threshold triggering mass slot eviction in the continuous batcher. The cascade produced multi-minute stalls for certain request classes, tail latency spikes up to 9x baseline for affected tenants, and severe fairness skew (priority inversion) between long-lived streaming requests and short text-generation RPCs. This ticket collects the follow-ups, long-term mitigations, and an operator playbook to prevent recurrence.
impact_summary: ~12:15–12:50 UTC on 2026-03-09: 6k requests (top 5% of traffic) experienced >95th percentile latency increase. Several enterprise customers observed degraded throughput and timeout retries. Autoscaler reacted but amplification from retries increased overall load. Business impact: degraded SLA for Dedicated tenants, two on-call escalations.

root_cause: A recently-deployed scheduler affinity heuristic (runtime-1.26-sched-v3) changed slot assignment ordering and inadvertently tightened the coordinator hard-stop threshold interaction with KV-cache eviction. Under high token velocity the coordinator triggered a mass eviction which prevented batch formation for affected classes. Retries and autoscale churn amplified load, producing a cascade. Secondary cause: insufficient per-class reservation and missing guardrails for admission control when eviction events occur.
mitigation_actions_taken: Rolled back runtime-1.26-sched-v3 affinity rollout to v2
Applied emergency override to raise hard-stop threshold on critical coordinators
Activated temporary admission control to deprioritize long-lived streaming requests
Restarted coordinator processes on three hotspots and purged stale KV-cache entries
Added short-term dashboard and PagerDuty alert for 'batch_formation_pause' metric

decisions: Rollback affinity change rather than patching in prod to stop immediate cascade (trade-off: delayed feature rollout)
Prioritize building admission control and per-shard reservations over aggressive scheduler heuristics for now
Implement canary synthetic burst test as a mandatory gate for scheduler changes
Favored rapid operational safeguards (dashboard + manual override) for short-term stability while long-term mitigations are implemented
